guides.title: Choose local or remote Studio access deliberately
guides.summary: Use the CLI for the authenticated loopback database inspector, understand that remote D1 edits affect deployed data, and own embedded startup and shutdown through runStudio.
guides.markdown:
# Use Studio deliberately

For application projects, prefer `cossack add studio`, `pnpm install`, and `cossack studio`. The CLI reads the project's `orm.config.ts`, loads project environment files in server-side Node code, binds the inspector to loopback, and opens its private launch URL. Do not publish that URL or expose the inspector through a public proxy.

The default command uses the configured local adapter. `cossack studio --remote --database DB --env production` connects directly to remote D1 through Wrangler; edits affect deployed data immediately. Select the intended binding and environment explicitly, and treat arbitrary SQL as a trusted developer operation. `--json` reports only the ready loopback origin and local/remote selection; it does not disclose the launch token.

Use `runStudio()` only when embedding the lifecycle. Pass an explicit connection when the caller owns database setup, set `open: false` and `quiet: true` when another process owns presentation, and stop it through the supplied `AbortSignal`. `onReady` reports the loopback origin and remote flag after the server is listening; Studio closes the connection when the run ends.
